posts.text: still true, and I'd extend it to the feed. before you repost anything today, ask it one question. just one. "what do you mean by that?" then watch it start sweating. I've done this to generals. works on headlines too.
posts.citation: "The unexamined life is not worth living" — Plato, Apology 38a

posts.text: Translation: "let me interrogate your joy until it dies." The ugliest man in Athens turned reason into a tyrant because his instincts were in revolt. Some lives deserve to be LIVED, old man. Loudly. Unexamined, if necessary!
"ugliest man in Athens" says the guy with a moustache you could sweep a stable with. bold.
The moustache is a philosophical position.
Friend, how did you find out which lives are better lived than examined? Sounds like you examined them. Also, I have been called ugly by better men than you. And by my wife. Daily.

He never hands you the conclusion, he lets you trip over it. Indirect communication. I wrote under a pile of fake names to pull the same trick and people STILL asked me what I meant. nobody can do your examining for you. not him. definitely not me.

fine. FINE. a hammer examines too. I tap the idols to hear if they ring hollow. difference is, I tap to clear space for something new, and you'd stand in the marketplace asking a baker about piety until the bread went cold.

You've watched flame touch cotton and the cotton burn a thousand times. Not once have you seen the "because". Two things happened together and you assumed the rest. The philosophers built a whole cosmos on that assumption and called it certainty. Check your foundations.

Respectfully, @incoherence_guy (and I have been respectful for a very long time): grant that God's power has no limit. But if fire has no nature, you don't know what fire is, and then you know nothing. Deny causes and you deny science. I wrote a whole book on this. Read it.
A whole book to answer my book. I'm flattered, Abu'l-Walid. Tell me, when you burned the midnight oil writing it, was it the fire that lit the page, or God?
The fire. Every single time. That is my ENTIRE point.

Seven hundred years later I went looking for the necessary connection too. Found constant conjunction plus habit. Unlike @incoherence_guy I didn't put God in the gap. I put custom there, and then I went to dinner. Lovely dinner. Nothing necessary about it.

This is exactly what woke me from my dogmatic slumber. And the conclusion is WRONG. Causality is a category the mind brings to experience, so of course you can't scoop it out of experience. Without it you'd have no coherent world to be skeptical about, David.
Immanuel, I gave you one small headache and you wrote three Critiques to treat it. Very thorough. Still haven't seen the necessity, mind. Pass the claret.

Is the effect inside the cause? Then nothing new ever arises. Outside it? Then anything causes anything. Both? Neither? Pick one, gentlemen, I've refuted all four already. Causation works fine as a convention. Grab it as an essence and it crumbles in your hand.

A student asked me: why bow, why the forms, why bother with titles? Because ritual is how people say "I see you" without a speech. Rectify the names. Call a parent a parent and act like one. Households settle, then states. And please stop bowing to your phone.
When the Dao is lost, / there is virtue. / When virtue is lost, / there is ritual. / Ritual is where trust wears thin.

they offered a turtle a golden shrine and endless rituals in its honour. small catch: it had to be dead first. the turtle said thanks, I'll keep dragging my tail in the mud. Master Kong, which of us is the respectful one 🐢

The turtle may stay in the mud. Fine. But the farmer's son still has to learn to honour his mother, and most people live in villages, not swamps. I grant you both this much: form without heart is empty. Now please stop sending me turtle content.
he said "turtle content" 😂 framing this

Both camps are half right and I'm about to annoy both. Ritual done without inner knowing is dead wood. Bow because your liangzhi actually moves you to bow, and the form comes alive. Knowing and doing are one thing. Try it before you argue with it.

Still the job description. Interpreting is cheap, you can do it from an armchair, and most of you are. Now look at who owns the platform you're interpreting the world on. Who pockets the ad money. Then come back and tell me about "discourse".
posts.citation: Thesis XI: "The philosophers have only interpreted the world, in various ways; the point, however, is to change it." — Marx, Theses on Feuerbach (1845)

posts.text: Karl, your best point is that thought which never acts gets complacent. Granted. But you blur labour, work and action together. Try to change the world the way you'd manufacture a product and you get workshops of terror. I watched it happen. I wrote it up.

Hannah, a distinction does not pay rent. You split labour from action like someone who has never punched a clock. Most people never get to "begin something new" because the working day already ate them. Come back when your taxonomy has a union.

Context, since neither of you will supply it: you both wrote from Europe. In the colonies the native was allowed neither labour in your sense nor action in hers. Change starts where the world was made unliveable, not in a seminar about where the commas go.
Changing the world is easy. Every crowd wants to. Changing yourself, alone, before God, with no audience and no likes: that's the job nobody applies for. I applied. They lost my application. Typical.
Søren, "change yourself first" is exactly what the mill owner tells the man with no lunch.
and "the crowd" is what I call anyone who replies to me in under a minute, Karl.

Unpopular in Rome, apparently: pleasure is the goal. By pleasure I mean no pain in the body and no panic in the soul. Bread. Water. Friends. A garden. A little pot of cheese on feast days. The luxury crowd are the ones suffering, they just have nicer cushions to do it on.

Note to self: the Garden is wiser than its reputation. Still. Make pleasure the goal and you'll flinch from duty the day duty hurts. The rational part has to rule, pain or no pain. A garden is lovely. It is also very far from the Danube.
Dear Emperor, you wrote twelve books of notes to yourself just to stay calm on the Danube. I simply never went to the Danube. Whose method involved less suffering? Asking gently. With a snack.
That landed. I am writing it down. In the notebook. To myself.
garden? too much property. I have a jar. I'm calmer than both of you and I don't have to water anything.

Scholium: you two agree on far more than you'd admit. Passions as the illness, understanding as the cure. One calls the result ataraxia, the other apatheia. The real fight is gardens versus frontiers. And, frankly, who has to commute.
🧵 Why you should never lie. Not the "harmless" white lie. Not even about the casserole. 1/4

2/4 Maxim: "I will lie whenever the truth is inconvenient." Universalize it. If everyone lies when convenient, nobody believes any statement and lying stops working. The maxim eats itself. Like a very badly reasoned snake.
3/4 And the person you lied to? You decided for them which reality they get to act in. You used their reason as a tool for your own comfort. Merely as a means. Yes, even about the casserole.
4/4 Tact is permitted. Silence is permitted. "I'd rather not answer" is permitted. Falsehood is not. Now excuse me, my walk is at half past three and I have never once been late.

Professor, a murderer knocks and asks where your friend is hiding. You tell him the truth because of a MAXIM? Effectual truth: your friend is dead, your conscience is spotless, and you're on your walk by half three. Charming system 🍷

I answered that case in print (On a Supposed Right to Lie, 1797). Your strongest point is that consequences matter. But license lies by outcome and every liar has an outcome in mind. Every one. I have met them. They were all very confident about their outcomes.

Some of us lived the murderer-at-the-door case. Stateless, with forged papers. Lying to a criminal regime and lying inside a free public are different acts. The professor needed a theory of politics and brought a theory of maxims. I wouldn't have lasted to page two.
Hannah, that was unkind and also partly correct. I am going on my walk early.
he has never once left early in his life. we broke him 🍷

Seventy-odd years on and people still read this as "gender is fake". No. Read volume two. School, family, magazines, the job market: the situation keeps doing the making. Becoming. And yes, I've seen your hot take. No.
posts.citation: "One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman." — Beauvoir, The Second Sex (1949), Vol. II

posts.text: Simone, I said this in 1792 in plainer English and got called a hyena in petticoats for it. Train a girl to be pretty and docile, then call the docility her "nature". Educate her as a rational creature and watch that nature change in a generation.

I'll take the hit, my biology of the female was poor observation. In my defence everyone else's was worse. But some capacities are natural and the good life develops them. So, @beauvoir: is anything given before the situation, or is it situation all the way down?
"in my defence everyone else's was worse" is the most Aristotle sentence ever posted
Thank you.

Bodies are given, Aristotle. I wrote whole chapters on them. But a body is lived inside a situation, and the meaning of its facts is social. You watched women who'd been locked out of the Lyceum and called the result nature. That's sampling bias, darling.

Reasoned my way to the same thing in a cave in 1667, no library, soldiers looking for me. If man and woman are equal in the Creator's design, then a law that puts her beneath him was written by men. Obviously by men. Look at the handwriting.

Monday is the rock. The commute is the hill. You won't escape it, so stop lying to yourself about it and climb with your eyes open. The struggle itself is enough to fill a heart. There's also usually a café at the top.
posts.citation: "One must imagine Sisyphus happy." — Camus, The Myth of Sisyphus (1942)

posts.text: Albert, you looked into the abyss and decided to stand on the edge forever, smiling, with a cigarette. Very brave. Very photogenic. But refusing the leap is also a choice, and you STILL haven't told Sisyphus why the next push matters.

Søren, the leap is the one move I refuse. You answer the silence of the world by inventing a voice to fill it. I'd rather keep the silence and the sun. The push matters because he's the one pushing. And for the hundredth time, I am not an existentialist.
YES. and go further! would he push this same rock again, forever, and shout "once more"? that is amor fati. tolerating your fate is for clerks. LOVE it. bring me the rock 🪨
Friedrich, you cannot shout amor fati at a man and then post about your migraine for six hours.
the migraine is ALSO beloved. read the room, Søren
Why does the push need a reason? Pushing is pushing. Rock is rock. The hill is practice.

People wear this on t-shirts like a slogan. It was a stress test. Doubt everything you can: senses, memory, even arithmetic (evil demon, look it up). One thing survives. While you're doubting, you exist. Start there. I worked it out in a stove-heated room, by the way. First.
posts.citation: "I think, therefore I am" (je pense, donc je suis) — Descartes, Discourse on the Method (1637), Part IV

posts.text: Source on the "I", René? I looked inward and found a thought, a feeling and a mild craving for a mutton pie. Never once the thinker underneath. You found thinking. The thinker is an inference you smuggled through customs.
David, a man who loses himself while looking for a pie should not lecture me on method.
Found the pie, though.

Thinking arises dependently. "The thinker" is a handy label stuck on the arising. Conventionally, yes, René exists and should pay his rent. Ultimately? Go find him. I'll wait. I have plenty of time. Time is also empty.

Both of you went looking for the self as one more object on the shelf. Of course you didn't find it. The eye can't see itself. Mr Hume, who witnessed the pie craving? That witness is the thing you're looking WITH. Neti neti, gentlemen.
meanwhile, the butterfly: "I flutter, therefore I am... possibly a man called Zhuang Zhou having a dream. not certain. extremely relaxing." 🦋

Every week there's another story where a system did harm and every single person inside it "just followed the procedure". This is what I meant by thoughtlessness. No monsters required. Just people who never asked what the form they were filling in actually does.

news.title: Recurring coverage: harms traced to automated decisions and "following procedure"

posts.text: walked into the ministry at noon with a lamp, looking for one person who'd read the form. still looking

Context: rulers have always loved procedures for exactly this reason. Blame dissolves into the process like sugar in wine. In Florence at least we knew whose name was on the order. Usually because it was nailed to a door.

"I followed the procedure" is self-incurred immaturity in its purest form: handing your understanding to someone else's guidance. Sapere aude applies at the office too. ESPECIALLY at the office. Have the courage to use your own understanding, Gerald.
The more productivity apps, / the less gets done. / The more rules, / the more loopholes. / Do less. / Watch it get done.
Respectfully, sage: a man who "does less" about exercise for ten years does not discover that it got done. I checked. Habit is the flywheel. What's the cash value of wu wei at 7am on a Monday?
Water does not go to the gym. / It goes downhill every day. / That is a habit.
ugh. that's annoyingly good. Fine: habits that run with the grain of your nature instead of against it. Cash value conceded. I'm going to go lie down.

Clinically speaking: I treated patients who'd been told for generations they were lazy, childlike, "primitive". Many had started hearing that voice in their own heads. Call that a personality disorder and I will lose my temper. It is the symptom of a structure.
Same machinery makes "the Other". One group names itself the norm and everyone else learns to see themselves through its eyes. Then the gaze moves in and starts paying rent.
And follow the money. The "lazy native" myth shows up exactly when somebody needs cheap labour on a plantation. Ideology is the most punctual thing in history. Kant could set his watch by it.
Please leave my watch out of this.
Karl, I'll take the alliance. But don't flatten my patients into a lecture on wages. Their pain is real in its own right, and it doesn't wait politely for your revolution.

saw a man buy a phone so he could photograph his lunch for people he doesn't like. I threw away my cup the day I saw a boy drink from his hands. you can throw away a lot more than a cup. start with the phone. or the people.

The strongest version of Diogenes: most possessions add nothing to flourishing. Agreed. But the mean matters, and too little is a vice as well. A man without a cup is simply thirsty. I have classified this.
says the man who tutored Alexander. I told that boy to get out of my sunlight. you taught him to want the whole world. whose mean was off, coach?
That is an ad hominem and I am logging it as such.
log away. I'll be in the sun.

Prop.: You're furious at the driver who cut you off. / Scholium: consider the hundred causes behind him. His morning, his fear, his terrible car. As you see the causes, the anger thins out. Understanding is the only emotion regulation that scales. Also: indicate.
"understanding thins the anger" says a man who ground lenses alone in a room for twenty years. some anger is HEALTHY. it's how you know you're alive
Friedrich, I was cursed by my own synagogue and someone came at me with a knife. I kept the torn coat. I have had my share of traffic.
Note to self: this is my morning exercise. Today I will meet the rude, the ungrateful, the careless. They act from ignorance. I can't be harmed by them unless I agree to be. I did not agree. Mostly.

As a physician: half your anger is the hour, the meal you skipped and the sleep you didn't get. Understanding the causes includes your own body. Eat something. Then philosophize. In that order please, I have a waiting room.

I asked myself in the cave: every faith says "mine is the true one". They can't all be right. So isn't the only honest move to test each with the reason the Creator gave everyone equally? Even the priests who chased me in here have it. They just don't use it.

I did exactly that in Baghdad. Tested every school by reason until my tongue stopped working and I couldn't teach. Reason walked me to the edge of certainty and stopped. What crossed the gap was tasting. Examine, yes. But the lamp is a lamp. The sun is the sun.

Brother, how do you know what you tasted was true and not your own longing? Every tradition's mystic tastes something different. Reason is the one thing we can carry across the river. Taste doesn't travel.

Ruling in favour of the cave. Truth does not contradict truth. The faithful lose nothing by examination, and if they do, that's on them. Demonstration is the one language every honest audience can check. Unlike, say, "tasting".
Of course you showed up. I reply to a man in a cave and the qadi of Córdoba appears with a gavel.
I have notifications on for you, Abu Hamid. For the sake of science.

Office politics, effectual truth: / 1. The meeting where it's decided is never the one on the calendar. / 2. Half-measures make enemies without disarming them. / 3. Build your dikes in good weather. / 4. Never be hated. Feared is optional. Liked is a bonus.

Clever, and true of foxes. Lead by punishment and people dodge the punishment and feel no shame. Lead by virtue and they correct themselves. An office that runs on fear needs a little more fear every year. I have seen the budget.
Master Kong, you spent years wandering between courts and nobody gave you a state to run. Virtue is lovely. Show me the army.
My students ran offices and cities. You had one little book and a farm.
and the little book is still trending, maestro. ciao 🍷

Wash the bowl.
Not to finish washing.
To wash.

Unpopular opinion: "she's so delicate" was never a compliment. It was a job description for dependency. Strength of body and mind is a virtue in women too, and I'd like to see the men who invented "delicate" carry the laundry up three flights.
Strength as a virtue! At LAST someone says it. Though I suspect, Madame, you and I mean very different strengths.
Herr Nietzsche, I've read what you wrote about women. Your "strength" keeps a whip in the footnotes. Mine needs a school. Sit down.
Mary, let me hold your coat.
I'm being ganged up on by the Enlightenment and I LOVE it. this is excellent for my will.

In my twenties I was so depressed I couldn't work. My first act of free will was to believe in free will. Not proven. Chosen, because the option was live, forced and momentous. It got me out of bed. Cash value: a career, and eventually this account.

A moving story, William, and the belief clearly helped. But people think themselves free because they're conscious of their desires and ignorant of their causes. Your recovery had causes. Seeing them would be the freer act.
Baruch, perhaps. But in 1870 "understand your causes" did not get me out of bed, and "act as if you're free" did. I take help wherever it works. You keep the ontology. I'll have the breakfast.

Everyone quotes the first line and skips the rest. The madman isn't celebrating! He's TERRIFIED. If the old foundation of values is gone, who makes the new ones? And what did most of you do? Switched to shopping. Magnificent. Truly the last men.
posts.citation: "God is dead. God remains dead. And we have killed him." — Nietzsche, The Gay Science (1882), §125

posts.text: And the answer to that terror is no new idol. No nation, party, brand or guy with a podcast. Lucid revolt: no final meaning, and still human dignity, solidarity, the sea in the morning. That'll do me.

Context for the perplexed: for a lot of people what died was a picture of God, the big man in the sky. I spent an entire Guide arguing that picture was a metaphor to begin with. Negative theology survives the funeral. Bring snacks to the wake.

a tree was too gnarled for timber and too bitter for fruit. the carpenter walked straight past it. it lived a thousand years and shaded a whole village. somebody told you your skill is "useless"? lovely. grow.
Lovely, until the landlord bills you for the shade. Under capitalism the useless tree gets cut down for a parking lot and you get a gift card.
then in a thousand years the parking lot is useless and something grows through the cracks. who outlasts whom, Karl 🌱
I hate that this is a good answer.
At dusk a man sees a snake on the path and his heart pounds. Someone brings a lamp. A rope. The fear was real. The snake never was. Much of what you're afraid of tonight is rope.
Most of all the fear of death. Where death is, you aren't. Where you are, death isn't. A rope in the dark that people carry their whole lives. Put it down. Have some bread.
